author: product-requirements-expert
title: Narrow the veterinarian directory to one specialty
summary: Both published forms of the veterinarian directory accept a named specialty in the request and bring back only the veterinarians holding it, matched on the whole name and disregarding letter case. The machine-readable form becomes a supported surface in the same slice.
acceptance_criteria: GET /vets.html?specialty=<name> renders the directory page listing only veterinarians holding that specialty; the listing stays paged over the narrowed set.
GET /vets?specialty=<name> returns the machine-readable veterinarian list carrying only veterinarians holding that specialty.
Matching is on the whole specialty name and is case-insensitive: 'RADIOLOGY' and 'radiology' match the same veterinarians; 'radi' matches none.
A specialty no veterinarian holds yields the ordinary page or the ordinary machine-readable document with an empty veterinarian list and HTTP 200, not an error and not a redirect.
A specialty value that is empty or whitespace-only behaves exactly as if the parameter were absent, the same way the existing empty owner search behaves.
Without the parameter, both /vets.html and /vets behave exactly as they do today.
Pagination links on the narrowed page carry the specialty parameter, so opening page 2 of a narrowed listing stays narrowed to the same specialty.
A veterinarian holding no specialty appears in no narrowed listing.
REQ-VET-003: the machine-readable list at /vets carries every veterinarian with the specialties each holds, and is covered by tests as a supported surface rather than an untested artifact.
Every behavior above is covered by tests.
non_goals: No form, dropdown, link, or any other page control for choosing a specialty on either surface. The narrowing is a request contract only in this slice; a visible control is a separate request, recorded as an open question in the PRD.
No free-text veterinarian search. NG-9 is narrowed, not retired: prefix or substring matching on a specialty or on a veterinarian name is out.
Naming more than one specialty in one request is undecided and out of this slice; implement exactly one.
REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its ID is never reused. The reinstated surface is REQ-VET-003.
No narrowing of pets or visits; neither is published as a list.
notes: Slice ships two REQs because REQ-VET-003 alone (make the machine-readable list a supported, tested surface) is 1-2 cycles and only makes sense alongside the filter it now carries; batched per the slice-sizing rule. The URL contract is product-owner-specified external surface, kept out of docs/prd.md prose to respect the PRD boundary rule (the PRD names no routes anywhere) - system-design-expert should record /vets.html?specialty=<name> and /vets?specialty=<name> in system-design.md#contracts. Two stale statements in docs/system-design.md are now wrong and are outside my write scope: line ~207 lists the machine-readable vet route as a known defect serving no requirement (it now serves REQ-VET-003), and line ~12 states there is no JSON API. docs/adr/README.md also needs an index row for adr/2026-08-23-non-goal-vet-free-text-search.md; that file is outside my write scope.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The narrowing extends the existing vet feature package in place: no new package, no new type, no service layer. Both published forms of the veterinarian directory keep the controller-to-repository shape recorded in system-design.md#package-structure. What is genuinely new and now recorded is (a) the machine-readable directory as a supported external contract rather than an artifact, and (b) a caching decision, because the narrowed read takes a caller-chosen string as a cache key in a cache with no bound and no eviction. docs/system-design.md gains a Contracts subsection naming both published addresses and the specialty parameter's meaning, and a new ADR records the no-cache decision.
integration_points: VetRepository gains two narrowed reads beside the two existing ones: a Page<Vet> variant for /vets.html and a Collection<Vet> variant for /vets. Derived query over the existing ManyToMany, matching specialties.name with Spring Data's IgnoreCase keyword (findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase; use the underscore form findBySpecialties_NameIgnoreCase if property resolution is ambiguous). Neither narrowed method carries @Cacheable.

VetController's two handlers each gain an optional specialty @RequestParam, normalize it at the web boundary (null or blank means unnarrowed, matching OwnerController's strip-and-treat-empty precedent), and branch to the narrowed or un-narrowed repository read. The normalized value goes back into the model so the page can carry it forward.

vets/vetList.html pagination links (five hrefs) currently build URLs by literal preprocessing '/vets.html?page=__${i}__'. They move to Thymeleaf's link-parameter form @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})} so the value is URL-encoded by the engine. Rendering specialty= empty when unnarrowed is acceptable, since blank is defined as equivalent to absent; omitting it entirely is preferable if the template stays readable.
No change to Vets, Vet, Specialty, the schema, or the seed data. The specialty column is untouched; matching is expressed in the query, not the schema.

patterns.description: optional-narrowing precedent: request value stripped, empty treated as the broadest read, paging preserved through the same helper
@DataJpaTest against the real repository and H2 seed data (radiology, surgery, dentistry) — the only seam that can demonstrate the query's matching semantics

risks.risk: Case-insensitive whole-name matching and the prefix non-match are properties of the generated SQL. A @WebMvcTest with a @MockitoBean VetRepository cannot demonstrate either — a stub returns whatever it is told, so those tests would pass against a wrong query.
risks.mitigation: Cover the matching semantics (whole-name equality, case-insensitivity, prefix matches nothing, unheld specialty yields empty) at the repository against the real database, in the ClinicServiceTests @DataJpaTest style. Keep VetControllerTests for parameter threading, blank-equals-absent, HTTP 200 on empty, JSON shape, and pagination-link carry-forward.

risks.risk: Owner search is case-sensitive under PostgreSQL because it leans on column casing behavior (Known Defects). Reaching for the same mechanism here would repeat that defect on a second surface.
risks.mitigation: Match through Spring Data's IgnoreCase derivation, which renders as a case-folding function on both sides of the comparison and holds identically on H2, MySQL, and PostgreSQL. Do not rely on the collation or column type.

risks.risk: Building the pagination href by string concatenation would put a caller-supplied value into a URL unescaped, opening attribute/markup injection on a page that is otherwise safe by Thymeleaf's default escaping.
risks.mitigation: Use the link-expression parameter form, never concatenation or the __${...}__ preprocessing currently in the template for the specialty value.

risks.risk: Adding @Cacheable to a narrowed read would key the unbounded, evictionless vets cache on an arbitrary caller string.
risks.mitigation: Decided: narrowed reads are uncached — docs/adr/2026-08-23-uncached-specialty-narrowed-vet-queries.md. The un-narrowed reads keep their annotations so today's behavior is unchanged.

risks.risk: Paging over a joined collection can push pagination in-memory if the query join-fetches the eager specialties.
risks.mitigation: A derived filter query joins for the predicate only; the eager specialties load by secondary select, so limit and offset stay in SQL, as they do for the existing paged read. If a Hibernate in-memory-pagination warning appears, that is the signal the query was written as a join fetch.

notes: Three stale-doc items flagged by product-requirements-expert were each verified and fixed. (1) Overview claimed no JSON API; it was qualified with 'for the primary workflows' but read as a blanket denial — reworded to name the one machine-readable surface and its requirement. (2) Known Defects listed the machine-readable vet route as serving no requirement — row removed, with a sentence recording why it left the list. (3) docs/adr/README.md was indeed missing an index row — added, along with a row for the new caching ADR. Also updated: the VetController, VetRepository, and Vets contract rows and their Implements column; a Persistence paragraph contrasting the two case-insensitivity mechanisms; the Security Context inputs line; a Threat Model row for caller-chosen cache keys; and Open Question 5, widened from invalidation to invalidation-and-bounds. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is empty. Open questions recorded rather than blocked, per the standing product instruction: whether the machine-readable form should also carry the narrowing in some envelope field (no — the PRD says only the veterinarians narrow), and whether an unnarrowed page's links should render specialty= empty or omit it (implementer's call, both satisfy the contract).

author: security-reviewer

findings.description: The XSS regression test asserts only a negative — the rendered page does not contain the literal '<script>'. That assertion also passes if the specialty stops being rendered into the pagination hrefs at all (for example a future refactor that drops the parameter, or a controller that stops putting it in the model), so it does not pin the encoding behavior it exists to protect. The encoding itself is correct today: I ran the class and it is green, and the ternary link-expression form makes Thymeleaf URL-encode the value before the attribute is HTML-escaped. The test is the weak link, not the code.
findings.fix: Add a positive assertion alongside the negative one, asserting the encoded value actually appears in a pagination href, e.g. .andExpect(content().string(containsString("specialty=rad%22%3E%3Cscript%3E"))). Keep the existing not(containsString("<script>")) assertion.

approved_aspects: No injection sink introduced: both new repository methods are Spring Data derived queries (findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase, with and without Pageable) bound as JPA parameters. A sweep of src/main/java for @Query, createQuery, createNativeQuery, and Statement finds only the pre-existing parameterless JPQL in PetTypeRepository — no string-concatenated JPQL or SQL anywhere in production code.

Reflected XSS in the pagination links is closed on all five hrefs. Each of vetList.html:35, :41, :47, :53, :59 is a ternary between two complete @{...} link expressions; the narrowed branch passes the value as a link parameter (@{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=${specialty})}) so the engine URL-encodes it, and the unnarrowed branch carries no caller input at all. The old '/vets.html?page=__${i}__' preprocessing form is gone from every href — a grep of src/main/resources/templates for __${ and th:utext returns nothing, so no other template concatenates or emits unescaped output.

The caller value is never echoed into the HTML body, only into href query parameters, and never into the JSON response. The only other 'specialty' identifier in the template (vetList.html:20) is a th:each loop variable over vet.specialties, scoped inside the table row and rendered through th:text — it does not shadow the model attribute at the pagination links.

Input normalization at the web boundary is safe and matches the OwnerController precedent: narrowingSpecialty strips the value and maps null/blank to null, so the un-narrowed path is byte-identical to today's behavior. No trust decision is derived from the value; it is only a query predicate.

The uncached decision in docs/adr/2026-08-23-uncached-specialty-narrowed-vet-queries.md is honored by the code: grep for Cacheable in src/main/java shows @Cacheable("vets") on exactly the two pre-existing findAll variants (VetRepository:45, :55) and on neither narrowed method, so no caller-supplied string ever becomes a retained cache key. The existing cache's key space is unchanged. The Threat Model row added at docs/system-design.md:204 states this accurately.

The reinstated JSON surface at /vets exposes no new data: Vets serializes Vet (id, firstName, lastName from Person) plus the eagerly-loaded Specialty names — exactly the fields the public /vets.html page already renders. No telephone, address, owner, or visit data is reachable from this endpoint, and the specialty parameter is not reflected into the response.

Supply chain: no build file is in the change set (build.gradle, gradle/libs.versions.toml, and the wrapper are untouched), so this slice adds no dependency and changes no version — no new CVE exposure to assess.
No secret-shaped literal in the diff. The only 'key'-adjacent additions are the cache-key discussion in the ADR and system-design prose; the test fixtures use vet names and specialty names only.

author: change-grader
summary: narrow the vet directory to one specialty

blast_radius.note: Twelve files but one feature package: two derived repository reads, both vet handlers, the vetList pagination links, plus docs and ADRs; no sensitive paths, no shared infrastructure, and the widest edit (all five pagination hrefs) is pinned by a test asserting the unnarrowed link still renders the same page-2 URL as before.

semantic_surprise.note: Read every prod hunk: narrowingSpecialty is null/strip/blank-to-null with no boundary trickery, both handlers branch on null to the existing unnarrowed reads, the narrowed queries deliberately skip the vets cache so a caller-chosen string cannot grow an unbounded cache, and specialties is EAGER so the new uncached reads survive open-in-view=false; the template ternary picks between two whole link expressions and never concatenates.

test_adequacy.note: Tests assert outcomes rather than restate the implementation: real DataJpaTest cases exercise whole-name match, case variants, prefix non-match, unheld specialty, and paging over the narrowed set (totalElements 2 with page size 1, the case a join-fetch pagination bug would break), MockMvc pins both surfaces plus the rendered carry-forward link, and the XSS test asserts both the encoded form present and the raw script tag absent.

reviewer_hedging.note: Round two is a clean unanimous approval from the full four-reviewer roster with no findings; round one's three findings were all autofix-tagged, all applied, and none was re-raised, with no escalate tag and no bar_clause anywhere in the slice.

scope_deviation.note: Zero consultations and zero build retries; the single design revision was a ledger-coverage correction adding docs/adr/README.md to supporting_paths, not a scope fight, and every changed path matches the intake file_targets or the superseding design block, including the PRD's NG-9 narrowing and REQ-VET-003 that the intake record itself authorized.

rationale: All five facets clear on a read of every hunk: the narrowing is contained, deliberately uncached, and covered by real database and MockMvc tests. Confirm and merge; at merge, ratify the documented NG-9 narrowing that makes the machine-readable list a supported surface.
